newsitem.title: USA: Alcan smelter boost gets mixed response.
newsitem.headline: Alcan smelter boost gets mixed response.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd's proposal to build a new aluminum smelter at its Kitimat complex in British Columbia, following the resolution of a two-year dispute with the provincial government, got a divided response from analysts.
While the proposed 225,000-tonne smelter would likely be absorbed by the market by 2003, the earliest start-up time, some questioned whether a focus on smelting capacity is the right move.

"By 2003, a new smelter would probably be needed," said Thomas McNamara, an analyst with Oppenheimer & Co. "What I would have liked to have seen was a focus on where their weakness is, which is raw materials. They have a lot to do on that side of the market."
Alcan is one of the higher cost producers of alumina, the precursor to high-grade aluminum.
"The possible Ely mine is far more interesting to me than new smelter capacity," he said.

Alcan is also planning to spend $130 million on a new bauxite mine at Ely, in the northern Australian state of Queensland, which would cost $130 million and would produce 2.5 million tonnes. It is expected to being production in the fourth quarter of 1999.
"I think the move is a very positive one for Alcan," said Clarence Morrison, an analyst with Prudential Securities. "This alleviates a potential supply (vacuum), particularly to the Asian markets.
"Alcan had a problem realizing value out of its Far Eastern investments," Morrison said. "This goes a long way towards addressing that."
Alcan is also planning to build a C$1.5 billion smelter in Alma, Quebec, which would produce 350,000 tonnes a year and would start in 2000 or 2001.
"It's not going to swing the market into an oversupply situation," Morrison said.
The company also plans to bring the exisiting smelter's production up to full capacity of 272,000 tonnes, up 22,000 from existing rates. Analysts said the increase would not have an immediate impact.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
